Difference in cell density between conditions on an embedding

Source: R/density_diff_plot.R
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit.Rd

Shows where on a 2D embedding (UMAP, tSNE, ...) the cells of a condition are enriched or depleted relative to a reference condition: the density of each condition is estimated with a Gaussian kernel, normalized so that cell numbers do not matter, and their difference is drawn on a diverging scale. One panel per compared condition, with a fixed size, as DimPlot_bioToolkit; save it with save_plot; the values behind it are returned by export_source_data.

Usage

DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
  object,
  split.by,
  reference = NULL,
  compare = NULL,
  sample.by = NULL,
  reduction = "umap",
  dims = c(1, 2),
  cells = NULL,
  full.extent = FALSE,
  measure = c("difference", "log2ratio"),
  draw = c("cells", "raster"),
  density.adjust = 1,
  n.grid = 256,
  mask.quantile = 0.05,
  cols = NULL,
  limits = NULL,
  na.value = "grey88",
  contour = FALSE,
  pt.size = 0.3,
  order = TRUE,
  label = FALSE,
  label.by = NULL,
  label.size = 3.5,
  label.color = "black",
  legend.position = c("right", "left", "top", "bottom", "none"),
  legend.title = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  arrow.panels = c("bottom.left", "all", "left", "right", "top", "bottom", "none"),
  panel.width = 4,
  panel.height = panel.width,
  panel.spacing = 0.1,
  raster = NULL,
  raster.threshold = 10000,
  raster.dpi = 1000,
  bg = "transparent",
  seed = 42,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object

split.by

Metadata column of the conditions (e.g. genotype)

reference

Level of `split.by` the others are compared with. If NULL (default), the first level

compare

Levels of `split.by` compared with `reference`, one panel each. If NULL (default), all other levels

sample.by

Metadata column of the samples. If given, one density is computed per sample and the densities of a condition's samples are averaged, so that every sample weighs the same and one large sample cannot drive the map. If NULL (default), the cells of a condition are pooled

reduction

Name of the reduction, default is "umap"

dims

Two dimensions of the reduction to plot, default is c(1, 2)

cells

Cells to use, as names or indices. If NULL (default), all

full.extent

Whether the axes span all cells of the object rather than only the plotted ones, default is FALSE

measure

"difference" (default): the compared density minus the reference density, divided by the reference's peak density; or "log2ratio": the log2 ratio of the two densities, with 1% of the reference's peak added to both

draw

"cells" (default): every cell coloured by the value at its position, masked cells in `na.value`; or "raster": the values on a grid, over the cells in `na.value`

density.adjust

Multiplier of the kernel bandwidth (Scott's rule on all plotted cells), default is 1. Larger values smooth more

n.grid

Number of grid points along each axis, default is 256

mask.quantile

Regions where both conditions are sparser than this quantile of the density at the cells' positions are masked (not coloured), default is 0.05

cols

Colours of the diverging scale: NULL (default) for "blue-magenta", a palette name, or colours from low to high, e.g. `c(low, mid, high)`

limits

Cutoff of the colour scale: it runs from -`limits` to `limits`, each end trimmed to the most extreme value drawn on its side, so that it gets the full colour. If NULL (default), from the lowest to the highest value drawn, centred on 0

na.value

Colour of masked cells, default is "grey88"

contour

Whether to draw contour lines of the density of all plotted cells, default is FALSE

pt.size

Size of the cells, default is 0.3

order

Whether cells with the largest absolute values are drawn on top, default is TRUE (`draw = "cells"`)

label

Whether to label groups of cells at their median position, default is FALSE

label.by

Metadata column of the labelled groups. If NULL (default), the active identities

label.size, label.color

Size and colour of the labels, default 3.5 and "black"

legend.position

Position of the legend: "right" (default), "left", "top", "bottom" or "none"

legend.title

Title of the legend. If NULL (default), the measure and the reference

ncol

Number of columns of panels. If NULL (default), all in one row

arrow.panels

Panels that get the dimension arrows: "bottom.left" (default), "all", "left", "right", "top", "bottom" or "none", as in DimPlot_bioToolkit

panel.width, panel.height

Size of each panel in inches, default 4; `panel.height` defaults to `panel.width`

panel.spacing

Gap between panels in inches, default is 0.1

raster

Whether to rasterize the cells: NULL (default) does so above `raster.threshold` cells per panel; or TRUE / FALSE

raster.threshold

Number of cells above which `raster = NULL` rasterizes, default is 1e4

raster.dpi

Resolution of rasterized cells, default is 1000

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent"

seed

Random seed of the drawing order of ties and of label placement, default is 42

...

Arguments passed to the dimension arrows, as in DimPlot_bioToolkit

Value

A ggplot object

Details

Cells without a value of `split.by` (or `sample.by`) are left out, with a message. All plotted cells set the bandwidth and the axis limits; cells of conditions that are not compared are drawn but do not enter the densities.

The map shows where the composition of the embedding shifts between conditions, not whether the shift is significant: embedding distances are distorted and cells are not replicates. Use a differential abundance test on samples (e.g. Milo) for that. With few samples per condition, consider `sample.by` so that one sample cannot dominate.

The source data (export_source_data) hold, for `draw = "cells"`, one row per cell and panel: `cell`, `panel`, `x`, `y`, `condition`, `value`, the normalized densities `density_reference` and `density_compare` at the cell, and whether it is `masked`; for `draw = "raster"`, the same per grid point.

See also

DimPlot_bioToolkit, FeaturePlot_bioToolkit, plot_composition_scatter

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Where are Mut cells enriched relative to WT?
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(obj, split.by = "genotype", reference = "WT")

# Every sample weighs the same; log2 ratio; group labels
p <- DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(obj, split.by = "genotype", reference = "WT",
                                sample.by = "sample", measure = "log2ratio",
                                label = TRUE, label.by = "cell_type")
save_plot(p, "density_difference.pdf")
} # }
